quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results (CEO Richard Blickman): revenue EUR 283.4 million, up 13.4% versus Q2 2026 and 113.6% versus Q3 2025, primarily on computing end markets with strength in hybrid bonding, photonics and data center applications; net income EUR 107.2 million, up 20.4% sequentially and 323.7% year over year; baseline opex fell from 32% of revenue in Q3 2025 to 16.4%. Year to date: revenue EUR 718.1 million (+69%), net income EUR 247.8 million (+179.1%), net margin 34.5% versus 20.9%, with gross margins helped by product mix and 'the pass-through of price increases to help offset higher supply chain cost'. Net cash EUR 246.6 million at September 30. The CEO said results 'indicate significant market share gains', particularly for Besi flip chip, multi-module die attach and hybrid bonding systems, and that automotive, industrial and non-AI computing markets saw 'some modest recovery'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue EUR 283.4 million (+113.6% YoY, +13.4% QoQ); net income EUR 107.2 million; YTD revenue EUR 718.1 million (+69%)

quarterly_data.signal: Orders (CEO Richard Blickman): Q3 orders EUR 342.6 million, up 17% versus Q2 and 96.1% versus Q3 2025, primarily on hybrid bonding, data center and AI-related mainstream computing applications including power management; orders for the last 12 months reached EUR 1.2 billion; year-to-date orders EUR 905.2 million, more than double 2025. He expects the 'favorable year-to-date order momentum' to continue in Q4, with strong demand for data center and photonics applications from Asian subcontractors and hybrid bonding capacity expansion planned by leading players for logic, CPO and edge AI devices; asked whether a digestion period is coming, 'we do not expect the momentum to decline', in both traditional assembly and hybrid bonding. Visibility is now 'a quarter, 2 quarters, 6 months, and for some programs, even longer', versus about a quarter to one and a half quarters in earlier years.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 orders EUR 342.6 million (+96.1% YoY); last-12-month orders EUR 1.2 billion; YTD orders EUR 905.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2026 guidance (CEO Richard Blickman): based on backlog and customer feedback, Q4 revenue is expected to be flat, plus-minus 5% versus Q3, 'as certain customers request delivery dates for third quarter 2026 received orders in alignment with H1 production capacity plans'; gross margin 63% to 65%; operating expenses up 5% to 10% versus Q3, primarily from strategic consulting cost. In Q&A he said it is 'not a customer push-out': orders of 'EUR 340 million something' ship across Q4, Q1 and Q2 depending on line and infrastructure readiness. A 16-week strategic review with key customers (and Applied Materials) on hybrid bonding, TC and mass reflow roadmaps for the next three to five years is four weeks in and should conclude in early January. Besi expects to grow 'more than double' the underlying assembly-equipment market growth rate.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue flat +/-5% QoQ; gross margin 63%-65%; opex +5%-10%

quarterly_data.signal: Hybrid bonding progress (CEO Richard Blickman): year-to-date hybrid bonding orders more than doubled versus fiscal 2025, as orders increased for HBM, more logic chiplet programs entered production, co-packaged optics use cases 'expanded faster than anticipated' and edge AI device production began; in 2026 hybrid bonding customer adoption grew to 23 customers and cumulative unit demand exceeded 215 systems. Q3 orders came from logic, co-packaged optics and memory customers, including both hybrid bonding and TC Next systems from a leading memory customer for development of current and next-generation HBM device structures. Besi is 'today shipping this quarter the first 50 nano' placement-accuracy (generation 2) systems, versus 100 for the 215 generation 1 and 1+ machines sold so far; 25 is under development, then 10. On CPO he cited 'a quite substantial order in the first quarter' and several in the last quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: hybrid bonding: 23 customers, cumulative demand more than 215 systems; first 50 nm systems shipping in Q4 2026

quarterly_data.signal: TC Next (CEO Richard Blickman): the thermo-compression platform now has seven customers, most of them logic so far; it is developed for bond pad pitches below 20 micron and fluxless processes, aimed at the next generation between 10 and 20 micron for memory stacking and logic (IMEC data showed results below 10 micron), and lets customers use a reflow process or hybrid bonding; 'in the next couple of years, it could be a very sizable product range'. The memory customer's TC Next order was a repeat order. Power management: automotive used to be 15% to 20% of revenue and has declined to 'somewhere around 10'; power for AI data center modules 'certainly brings that back' to those levels.
quarterly_data.figure: TC Next: seven customers; sub-20 micron bond pad pitch

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and customers (CEO Richard Blickman): Besi grew nearly 70% year on year with its supply chain and operating model, which lets it increase capacity rapidly; longer lead times of other tools in customer lines delay shipments of orders. A U.S. logic customer that placed a large volume order in 2024, shipped and installed in 2025, is in 'full preparation now for mass volume production', and 'one can expect further expansion in next year', with plans to also set up operations in Asia close to Besi's manufacturing. Asked about the leading GPU player adopting hybrid bonding (qualification this year, orders next year, volume in 2028), he said 'the timeline is still more or less as you have remembered', with volume hard to predict. China remains a long-term growth market spanning many subcontractors, high-end smartphone assembly, TC and hybrid bonding development and pluggables; demand for pluggables (EVO) continues, 'directly related to data centers'.
quarterly_data.figure: growth of nearly 70% year on year in capacity / shipments

players.product: hybrid bonding and thermo-compression bonders for die stacking

quarterly_data.signal: HBM hybrid bonding view (CEO Richard Blickman): severe memory shortages in 2026 extended the use of lower stack heights in current HBM production beyond prior expectations, but the need for power efficiency, bandwidth, interconnect density and speed 'has only increased interest' in hybrid bonding for HBM; Besi anticipates adoption 'in a range of stack heights over the next two years' and new stacks combining HBM, custom advanced logic base dies and direct bonding of DRAM onto accelerator chips by decade end. Development for HBM stacking 'is continuing at full speed with all three memory manufacturers'; timing of mainstream volume is set by their end customer, and feedback from customers testing hybrid bonded HBM samples is 'very positive'.

connects_to.relationship: partnership on automated line concepts combining BESI hybrid bonding with Applied Materials equipment for memory (HBM) applications

contracts.signal: CEO Richard Blickman: Besi was recently included as an innovation partner at Applied Materials' EPIC Center (Sunnyvale), showcasing Besi hybrid bonding and TC Next solutions; the relationship with Applied goes back seven years and 'the first program we will set up is both for hybrid bonding and TC for a major U.S. customer'. Applied Materials is also involved in Besi's 16-week strategic review.
